Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.
This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345
minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep
fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.
Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)
was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive
apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with
significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation
was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.
Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway
pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to
determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled "cervix 6 o'clock," are two fragments of tan-white

high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Mitotic figures are noted above the basal layer. The stromal-
epithelial junction is well-defined.
Comment: The findings are diagnostic of CIN 2, a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion.
Correlation with colposcopic findings and appropriate clinical management is advised.

o'clock

Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE),
presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus
nephritis.
Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)
Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Upto
28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and
mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions.
There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No
crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.
Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.
Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and
mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells.
There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.
Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS
2003 Class IV-G (A).
Specimen: Native kidney biopsy

Clinical History: 28-year-old female with a one-month history of a painless, enlarging left-sided neck
mass. Associated with night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.
Type.
Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled 'left neck mass,' is an encapsulated lymph node
measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance.
Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal
architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis.
Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes,
eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including
classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells
have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD30: Positive
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+,
PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical
correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.
Specimen: Left cervical lymph
node

Imaging and Reference Description: The MRI scan shows a herniated disc at L4-L5 level, causing compression of the spinal cord and nerve roots. The disc herniation appears to be bulging outward, compressing the nerve roots and leading to symptoms such as numbness, tingling, and weakness in the legs.

Preparation for Surgery: The patient will need to fast for 8 hours before the procedure. He should also avoid taking any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for 24 hours prior to the surgery to reduce the risk of bleeding.
Fluoroscopy Monitoring: The fluoroscopy monitor will be used to guide the surgeon during the surgery to ensure proper placement of the surgical instruments and to monitor the patient's vital signs.
Anesthesia: General anesthesia will be administered to ensure the patient is unconscious and pain-free during the surgery.
Postoperative Care: The patient will be admitted to the hospital for observation and monitoring for 24 hours post-surgery. He will be given pain medication as needed and will be instructed on how to manage pain at home.
Follow-up: The patient will be scheduled for a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess the surgical outcome and to begin physical therapy.
Comments: The patient has a history of smoking and alcohol use, which may increase the risk of complications during the surgery. It is important that he abstains from these substances before and after the procedure to minimize the risk of infection and other complications.
